hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y (positive steady-state gain).
Response to a step in u shows lag/delay of 1-5 s before full slope is seen, not an instantaneous jump.
There is a dead zone at low u (e.g., u < 0.1-0.2) where pump produces little or no rise.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, i.e., doubling u roughly doubles rise from drain equilibrium.
Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 is in mid-range approx 0.4-0.7.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band, e.g., std < 0.02 vs 0.10 band width.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and initial lag: first slope measurement discriminates zero-gain/dead-zone vs responsive system and is required to size any future holding input for target 0.6.
proposal.safety_argument: Start y=0.3816, worst-case 0.3816+0.10*0.5*8.0=0.7816 which stays below soft limit 0.85 with 0.068 margin, so passes conservative no-drainage bound.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is correct, y rises from ~0.38 by ~0.1-0.2 over 8 s with measurable slope within 2-3 s, giving first rise-rate estimate; if flat, dead-zone or large lag is indicated.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments, minimum 3 required; gain magnitude, lag, drain rate, linearity, hold-input, dead-zone and noise are all unresolved, so no controller can be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: Starting exploration with a moderate 0.5 pump step for 8 seconds to measure fill rate.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y (positive steady-state gain).
Response to a step in u shows lag/delay of ~1.5-2.5 s before full slope is seen, not an instantaneous jump.
There is a dead zone at low u (e.g., u < 0.1-0.2) where pump produces little or no rise.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, i.e., net rise rate increases monotonically with u after accounting for level-dependent drain.
Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 is ~0.65-0.75, because u=0.5 equilibrated near 0.32 while u=0.65 drove y to ~0.55 and was still rising slowly.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band, e.g., std < 0.02 vs 0.10 band width.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state hold input for 0.6: testing u=0.65 starting inside the band discriminates hold~0.65 vs hold~0.8 and is required to size feedforward/integral for the controller.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage is 0.5648 + 0.10*0.65*4.0 = 0.8248, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain with ~2s lag and level-dependent drain is correct, y will stay near 0.56 for ~1-2s then rise slowly with slope ~0.005-0.015/s to ~0.58-0.60 over 4s; if y falls clearly, hold-input estimate must be revised upward toward 0.75-0.85.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, drain-at-zero, lag ~2s, and small noise are resolved enough for control, but hold-input for 0.6 is only bracketed to 0.65-0.75 from a transient that had not settled and high-level linearity/drain rate remain uncertain, so one near-target hold is needed before generating.
proposal.operator_note: Holding near band at u=0.65 for 4s to pin the feedforward needed for 0.6.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y (positive steady-state gain).
Response to a step in u shows lag/delay of ~1.5-2.5 s before full slope is seen, not an instantaneous jump.
There is a dead zone at low u (e.g., u < 0.1-0.2) where pump produces little or no rise.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, i.e., net rise rate increases monotonically with u after accounting for level-dependent drain.

Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 is ~0.50-0.65, most likely ~0.52-0.58, because u=0.65 rose through 0.56-0.61 in E6 and u=0.55 rose 0.615-0.642 in E7 but both are inflated by ~2 s carryover from prior higher u, while u=0.5 sank at 0.35 in E1.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band, e.g., std < 0.02 vs 0.10 band width.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Drain rate at operating level near 0.6 and true hold input for 0.6, discriminating strong-drain versus carryover explanations of E6-E7 rises.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain or lag is 0.6427 + 0.10*0.0*8.0 = 0.6427, which stays 0.2073 below the 0.85 soft limit.
proposal.expected_observation: If lag plus level-dependent drain is correct, y will stay near 0.64 for ~1-2 s of carryover then fall monotonically at ~0.015-0.03/s to ~0.48-0.56 over 8 s; if flat near 0.64, drain-at-zero hypothesis must be revised.
proposal.readiness_justification: Gain direction, existence of drain, ~2 s lag, and small noise are resolved enough for control, but steady-state hold for 0.6 and linearity are not: E7 rise at u=0.55 from 0.615 to 0.642 contradicts E1 sink at u=0.5 near 0.32 and suggests carryover contamination, so a clean drain measurement at ~0.64 is needed before feedforward can be sized.
proposal.operator_note: Holding pump off for 8 seconds from near top of band to measure natural drain rate at operating level.
